title: The Shipwrecked Man and the Sea

keywords: the shipwrecked man and the sea
full_text:
A merchant whose ship was shattered in a terrible storm managed to drag himself onto the sandy shore, barely escaping drowning. Exhausted and bitter at the loss of all his cargo, he sat upon the beach and cursed the Sea, calling her treacherous, merciless, and a trap for mankind.

The Sea took the form of a majestic woman rising from the foam and addressed the weeping mariner:

"Do not lay the blame for your ruin at my door, wanderer! Look upon me: of my own nature, I am calm, tranquil, and clear as glass, gently bearing ships upon my breast. It is the violent Winds that fall upon me with fury, stirring my waters into mountains of foam and driving ships onto rocks. Blame the storms that incite the strife, not the calm element that is stirred against its will!"
moral: Do not blame the instrument for the violence of the tempest that stirs it.

quiz.question: What is the central moral lesson taught in "The Shipwrecked Man and the Sea"?

Believing rumors and flattery without proof

quiz.question: What memorable conclusion does this story teach young readers?
